the question of whether it is possible to design a classifier that requires optimal resources to classify correctly.
the question of why we need a neural network that has millions of parameters to classify speech or image.

In the context of deep neural networks, fixing the classifier weights while training the network can lead to significant performance improvements.
the authors have presented a novel and practical way to keep the computational power of a neural network while avoiding its overfitting.
the proposed approach is a practical and effective way to improve the performance of neural networks for the task of classification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we simply use the last layer of the network to train a classifier and then remove the classifier to train the rest of the network for a better representation of the data.
we are fixing the size of the output layer, but at the same time we increase the number of classes through learning.
the marginal value of the last classifier layer, while increasing linearly with the model capacity, ends up decreasing exponentially by using an Outrageously Large Neural Network.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can replace the classifier of a neural network with a single, linear, fixed-width layer and retain relatively high accuracy while making the network significantly smaller (the input image dimensions are also reduced with a simplification of considering the original affine transforms as an additive constant).
we can reduce the number of parameters required for a classifier while maintaining performance, thus making classifiers much more computationally efficient.
we can reduce the representation complexity in a learned classifier without losing generalization performance by applying a single weight change to the learned classifier.
